sections.title: Shared case store, loading and hooks
sections.what: Holds the browser-side case store, the case state types, the provider that loads and saves cases, and the hooks screens use to read a case and run actions.
sections.why: Likely reason: one store shared across screens avoids duplicate loading and keeps the language consistent.
sections.watch_out: Using a hook outside the provider throws an error, so every screen that uses them must sit inside the provider.

summary: Provides shared case data to the screens, loads and stores cases in the browser, and reloads them when the language changes.
purpose: Lets screens show case details and run actions such as creating a case, attaching a sample document and processing it, without each screen repeating the logic.
why: Likely reason: one shared store avoids each screen fetching the same case separately.
how: Defines a case state that is loading, ready with details and a language, not found, or error. Creates a React context that holds the cases and actions. The CaseProvider component keeps the cases in state, reads the current language, saves each loaded case and exposes loading and action functions that wrap the case service. The shouldLoadCase rule decides when to fetch. The useCaseDetail hook runs that rule in an effect and returns the state. The useCaseActions hook returns the action functions.
inputs: A case identifier from the screen, and the input needed to create a case.
outputs: The case state for screens and the results of the actions.
risks: Hooks throw an error if used outside the provider. Cases are held in browser memory, so a page refresh clears them. The loading step is partly cut off in the packet.
debug: If a screen stays on loading, check the state and whether the case service call failed. If a hook throws, check the screen sits inside the provider.
